title: (CEN- CONFISCATION, EXPROPRIATION, NATIONALIZATION)
summary: The document is a Political Risk Insurance policy schedule for investors, covering Confiscation, Expropriation, and Nationalization (CEN). It includes a schedule with fields for policy number, insured details, countries involved, liability limits for three insuring agreements, policy periods, currency, premium, insured percentage, waiting periods, deductible, and intermediary details. It also contains the insured's representations, entire agreement clause, endorsement count, broker details, signature block, and Tata AIG's contact and registration information.

title: (CEN- CONFISCATION, EXPROPRIATION, NATIONALIZATION)
key_items: A. INSURING AGREEMENT I:; B. INSURING AGREEMENT II:; C. INSURING AGREEMENT III:
summary: This document is a Political Risk Insurance policy for investors issued by Tata AIG General Insurance Company Limited, covering Confiscation, Expropriation, and Nationalization (CEN). It includes a policy number placeholder and a preamble stating that coverage is provided in consideration of premium payment and reliance on the insured's statements, subject to the schedule, endorsements, terms, conditions, and limitations. The policy contains three insuring agreements: I) indemnification for loss caused by an Expropriatory Act by the Host Country Government; II) indemnification for loss from a Nontransfer condition lasting the Waiting Period; and III) indemnification for loss from damage or destruction of the Foreign Enterprise's physical assets due to Political Violence in the Host Country. The document also provides the company's contact information and registration details, including registered office address, 24X7 toll-free number, fax, email, website, IRDA registration number, UIN, product code, and CIN.

title: ARTICLE II. CAUSES OF LOSS
key_items: A. EXPROPRIATORY ACT; B. NONTRANSFER; C. POLITICAL VIOLENCE
summary: ARTICLE II defines three causes of loss: Expropriatory Act (government acts like expropriation, confiscation, nationalization, requisition, or sequestration that permanently deprive the Insured of shareholding, the Foreign Enterprise of assets, prevent operations causing total cessation, or deprive the Insured of inventory/equipment in the Host Country); Nontransfer (inability to convert and transfer funds outside the Host Country through normal channels to remit earnings or repatriate the insured Investment in Policy Currency); and Political Violence (violent acts including Rebellion, Insurrection, Civil Commotion, Riot, Terrorism, Strike, or Sabotage, and violent acts for labor objectives). The page also includes Tata AIG General Insurance Company Limited's contact and registration information.

title: ARTICLE III. DEFINITIONS
key_items: A. CIVIL COMMOTION; E. GOVERNMENT OF THE HOST COUNTRY
E. GOVERNMENT OF THE HOST COUNTRY
summary: ARTICLE III. DEFINITIONS defines key terms for an insurance policy, including Civil Commotion, Date of Loss for three Insuring Agreements, Deductible, Foreign Enterprise, Government of the Host Country, Guarantee, Insured Percentage, Insurrection, Investment, Maximum Limit of Liability, detailed Loss calculations for each Insuring Agreement (including asset valuation methods), Net Investment computation, Policy Currency, Policy Period, Rebellion, Riot, Sabotage, Strike, Terrorism, and Waiting Period.

title: ARTICLE IV. EXCLUSIONS
summary: Article IV outlines exclusions where the Company is not liable for loss. It excludes nuclear-related risks (radiation, contamination, weapons); non-compliance with Host or Insured's Country laws (environmental, health, safety), with Insured's Country law prevailing; environmental contaminant release; breach of representations or wrongful acts by Insured/Foreign Enterprise; financial defaults, currency issues, and contractual obligations; property damage except willful government destruction or Political Violence; war between five major powers; transfer restrictions and fund conversion failures; road accidents, arms handling, strikes; contract delays or cancellations; theft and inventory shortages; transit losses under specific insurance; government public interest measures; war/civil unrest; and computer failures including Y2K-related data processing issues.

title: ARTICLE V. WARRANTIES AND COVENANTS
summary: Article V outlines the Insured's warranties and covenants, including: no prior knowledge of loss circumstances and truthful information; duty to minimize loss, cooperate in investigations, and avoid settlements without consent; compliance with licensing and laws (with Insured's Country law prevailing in conflicts); no awareness of currency transfer delays or restrictions; confidentiality of the policy; truthfulness of written statements with consequences for misrepresentation; preservation of legal remedies; retention of uninsured risks; prompt claim notification within 30 days with potential Waiting Period termination; and maintenance of property/builders risk insurance for Foreign Enterprise assets.

title: ARTICLE VI. PROOF AND PAYMENT OF LOSS
summary: This article outlines the conditions for payment of loss: payment is made after the waiting period in Item 10 of the Schedule, provided that satisfactory written proof of loss is submitted to the Company, such proof is submitted within 12 months of the Date of Loss or within 30 days if demanded by the Company, and the loss is caused by an insured peril. The Insured bears the responsibility for proving the loss. The text also includes company identification and contact information.

title: ARTICLE VII. GENERAL CONDITIONS

nodes.title: A. Accounting Principles
nodes.summary: Article VII covers general conditions: accounting principles requiring financial statements and loss calculations to follow generally accepted accounting principles in the Insured's Country; arbitration procedures detailing dispute resolution via sole or three arbitrators, cost sharing, location, language, applicable law, condition precedent, and fallback to Indian courts; assignment requiring Company's written consent and endorsement; cancellation terms allowing either party to cancel with 30 days notice and specifying premium adjustments; and includes Tata AIG company contact and registration details.

nodes.title: B. Arbitration
nodes.summary: Article VII outlines general conditions including accounting principles, arbitration procedures, assignment rules, cancellation terms, changes requiring written endorsement, choice of Indian law and courts, compliance requirements, conformity to statutes, integration of schedule and proposal, consequences of fraudulent statements, and reference to insured's records.

nodes.title: Insurance Policy Terms: Changes, Law, Compliance, Fraud, and Schedule
key_items: E. Changes; F. Choice of Law and Forum; G. Compliance by Insured; J. False or Fraudulent Statement, Reports or Claims, Concealment
F. Choice of Law and Forum
J. False or Fraudulent Statement, Reports or Claims, Concealment
nodes.summary: The page outlines insurance policy provisions: premium refund conditions and cancellation effectiveness; changes require written endorsement; choice of law and forum is India; compliance by insured must be excused in writing; conformity to statutes amends conflicting terms; the Schedule and proposal are integral; false or fraudulent statements or concealment void the policy and forfeit claims; and includes a section heading for Insured's Records plus company contact and registration information.

nodes.title: K. Insured's Records
nodes.summary: The text outlines policy provisions regarding premium refunds (none if a claim is made), cancellation conditions, the requirement for written endorsements for changes, governing law (India) and forum (Indian courts), compliance and conformity to statutes, the integral nature of the Schedule and proposal, consequences of fraudulent statements or concealment (void policy), the company's right to examine insured's records, a 24-month limitation period for actions against the company, payment options for loans in non-policy currency, written notice requirements, excess insurance clause, and the allocation of recoveries from third parties.

nodes.title: Policy Provisions on Limitation, Loans, Notices, Other Insurance, Recoveries
key_items: L. Limitation Period for Action Against the Company
M. Loans Not Denominated in Policy Currency
nodes.summary: The page outlines several policy provisions: the Company's right to examine and copy documentation and obtain third-party information; a 24-month limitation period for actions against the Company; options for compensation payment when loans are not in policy currency; requirements for written notices; a clause making this insurance excess over other valid insurance; and rules for recoveries, where recovered sums reimburse the Company first, with excess going to the Insured. It also includes page number and company contact details.

nodes.title: Q. Subrogation
nodes.summary: The text covers subrogation conditions, including the Company's rights to recovery and the Insured's duties to assist and avoid prejudice, as well as assignment of currency rights for losses under Insuring Agreement II and salvage handling. It also outlines renewal terms, stating renewal requires consent, may involve changes, and terminates if not renewed, with specific receipt requirements. Finally, it includes the policy signing details and Tata AIG company information, such as address, contact, and registration numbers.

title: Customer Grievance Redressal Procedure
summary: The text outlines Tata AIG General Insurance's customer grievance redressal procedure, including initial complaint channels (24x7 toll-free number, email), nodal officer contact via website, and response timelines (10 days for initial, 8 days for escalation level 1, 7 days for escalation level 2). It details escalation contacts and the option to approach the Insurance Ombudsman within 30 days if unsatisfied. It provides the company's registered office and contact details, a comprehensive list of Insurance Ombudsman offices with their addresses, phone numbers, fax, email, and jurisdictions across various Indian cities and regions. Additionally, it includes regulatory information: policy subject to IRDAI regulations, a disclaimer on prohibition of rebates under the Insurance Act 1938 with penalties, a note on solicitation, and that risk cover commences upon premium receipt.
